ateret-zekenim/3:_: A sack full of flour on which chickens sat and it became moist from their droppings—one should sift the dough outward and the rest is permitted. (Beit Yosef in name of R' Eliezer of Garmiza)
ateret-zekenim/4:_: He should take in his hand and afterward must sift all the remaining flour (Maharshal); and so is the custom. Flour in a sack that mice bit—its law is likewise: if before Passover one must sift the flour; if crumbs like dry dough crumbs remain on the sieve they are discarded and the flour may be retained until after Passover. If found thus on Passover it is forbidden for benefit and sifting does not help. If the sack rests in its place without shaking and the flour did not mix, he takes in his hand the bitten place and ties the sack there under the bite with some flour; the remainder may be retained by sifting; nevertheless it is forbidden to eat on Passover. All this only when it appears the mice ate some of the flour; but if they bit only the sack and there is doubt perhaps they ate nothing—even if found on Passover it may be retained and is forbidden to eat; even if found thus before Passover, lest there is chametz that dried and crumbles. (My teacher in Bach siman 453) But the Gaon Maharam of Lublin wrote in responsum siman 119 that they should take other guarded flour to make matzot for the first two nights, and flour from mouse bites they should make matzot and bake all those matzot before Passover by sifting the flour; and that sieve through which they sifted the flour—one need not be stringent and it is permitted for everything:
biur-halacha/3:_: Sack full of flour that became moist—Pri Chadash wrote: sack full of flour buried in sand and flour found moist is chametz, for we learned chapter 3 Machshirin: burying in sand is in ki yutan; Raavad wrote there is no sand without water:
biur-halacha/4:א: And if impossible, etc., sift flour, etc.—this is Rokeach's view; although Rosh wrote on this view it is great leniency, Mechaber relied since Mordechai agrees—only when dried Mordechai also stringent like Rosh; Mechaber ruled stringently not like Rokeach. See Netziv and Magen Alef who appear not to have decided this:
biur-halacha/4:ב: And if dried on Passover, etc.—see Mishna Berurah. Shulchan Aruch implies even if sifting was on Passover may retain; Magen Alef doubts since mixing occurs through sieve holes—why permit retain? Source in Beit Yosef also requires sifting before Passover [if not sifted before Passover throw all—but no difference dried before or on Passover, only before Passover advice to sift]; Pri Megadim also strained; Magen Alef agreed Mechaber means dried before Passover has remedy by sifting, on Passover no remedy, forbidden to retain; only manner of speech that before Passover they are careful to sift—end:
biur-halacha/5:א: (1) and leg water - see MB here in the Mishnah Dasharin 5 Ita and leg water between large and small and the Rash and the Rabbi interpreted between large from a machin that comes out of the anus and here it seems to be a contradiction why the DKIL does not leave a dish of chickens and animal dung and that is why the column rules that a dash of flour on which chickens have sat and become moist from their matzah is not chametzed the moist flour there [see In the 28th and 16th] and I found in the A.R. Shemterz was smeared with thick excrement and it seems that there is no knoken that it is really thick so that the flour in the bag was moistened and a dough was made by the roosters throwing excrement on it from above, but it was not completely soft. And in the BA I saw that he wrote two opinions on the matter of soft excrement, 11. Dedino is like fruit water and 1.1. Dainu misses it at all, and here is the second 1.1 simply that it is the opinion of the arbitrators, that it is sealed, 1.1. It is very doubtful that it is known what made it difficult for Rabbi Daha Tanan in Sipa to drink the water of Tiberias, but that their clean exits are not considered a drink again since they exited through the anus, and look at that name, which is very repressed in its argument, and the evidence that he brought there for his explanation is not proven at all. And if it weren't for the interpretation of the Rash and the Rabb, the above would have simply been a distinction between the one who has legs and the one who has a person's feet. Big and whether it is a small one, since it is sustainable and apoki if it is only eight months old, as I have pointed out in the Mishnah that follows it, later I found in Rambam in the Laws of Impurity of Eating, which copies the law of the Mishnah, and it seems the simplicity of his words, which he interprets according to our words [and refer to the answer of the second thread, mark L. that he interprets the words of Rambam 33 according to our words], as well as in the Ar on the order of purity attributed to the Hagra Bahadiya interprets according to our words and we simply deviated from the Rash's interpretation because of the difficulty of the Toitat and here the PZ even soft as water literally as a ruling as excrement for this matter and in the answer to the second thread above is on the side of saying that even the interpretation of the Rash and the Rabb does not have the term in the Mishnah for soft excrement to be a ruling like foot water for the purpose of kosher drinking the water of Tiberias. That is, through the anus, and according to his words, we do not now have any opinion about feces that are as soft as water, which would be as important as foot water for the sake of kosher, and in any case, the Omnipresent for the sake of acid. However, 27 we wrote per the opinion of the arbitrators, that the matter of pickling for the purpose of kosher is considered kosher. [Refer to the AR] And yet, by joining another doubt, surely it should be alleviated as follows:
biur-halacha/5:ב: And human sweat—see Mishna Berurah. On chicken droppings, Maamar Mordechai 104 ruled one who bought wheat sack found dry cat droppings—permitted for Passover; though one should not learn from chicken droppings in Rokeach—birds differ for no urine concern as non-nurslings lack urine place (Shaarei Shamayim maamar 4); cats one may fear urination like dung placed there and chametzed—nevertheless do not establish prohibition; perhaps no urine or far from wheat or perhaps not chametzed; even if slightly chametzed only minority of minority; urine law disputed in Beit Yosef; Pri Chadash and Chafetz Chayim: only human urine chametzs—without visible spoilage in wheat do not be stringent else no grain without this doubt—primary—end:
chokhmat-shlomo/3:_: Section C. A bag full of flour moistened by the sweat of the wall is allowed, etc. P.S. Refer to the MS column on dry meat that sweats that is sour and refer to the MGA above, C. 17B, which wrote that the taste is stronger when it sweats, the water is pulverized, and it is in the eye of the S. and the meaning is because it was washed away by water, so the water was swallowed by it, even though we were dried later, when the sweat comes back and emits, and here I was satisfied if the first wash was removed with water and the last wash was removed with fruit water Sat Damhani wash off with fruit water for the last time, and then the meat is dried and it returns to sweat, whether or not it misses a nima who sweats only from the last of the fruit juices and does not miss, or a nima who sweats from the first alone and oh water or he sweats from this and that and oh fruit juice with water and oh stiff chametz ACP. And here it seems that this rule is an explicit Mishna in the PB Darla Mig and Zal Kelik who sprinkles with impure oil and repeats and sprinkles with pure oil or who sprinkles with pure oil and repeats and sprinkles with impure oil RA O' After the first I come and the sages say after the last and refer to Rambam and the Rash and the Rab who interpreted that is when they both dry then when he sweats afterwards and emits to RA Amarinan who emits the first and the sages Amirinan that emits the last one and Anan K.L. as sages, it is proven that if he swallows one after the other, only the last one is not emitted, since he was flushed out with fruit water, he does not emit only the fruit water, not the water of the first flush, and therefore he does not miss, as the above is true and clear. And the body of this thing about dry meat that the column inserted in the middle of the RA's words from Germiza Tsa that the Rabbi brought these words in the name of the RA and these words about dry meat he did not bring at all and these words of the column They are copied from the words of the Rash in the PB, and why did he put in the middle of these things that the Rash didn't write, and if they are explained in the pharmacist himself, why did the Rash omit it, and if not the Sal, then why did the column judge and check a little:
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: (There seif 4) water on flour or sack moistened, etc.—see Chok Yaakov lenient, proof from chapter 9 Parah. Rav Nachum Ginzburg Kraske wrote: reject proof—distinguish drinking vs eating—drinking swallows without chewing saliva; eating different—brief. I answered Chafetz Chayim proof correct: if mouse expels saliva from mouth, at least doubt expelled before/after drinking; known vermin have no saliva—if rely on this estimate even with impurity presumption, more so here no prohibition presumption but permission presumption—Chafetz Chayim correct for law—end:
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: [a] Not to chew, etc. It means that it is permissible for the chewer and the swallower to chametz immediately (Magan Avraham), and this is the tongue of bread that changes a chapter every hour, as long as it is chewed and engaged in chewing, I will not leave it to chametz, and from this it seems to me that it is permissible to eat dough that has not been left unbaked until this point. And in Ramban's answer, the sign of KG and the Rashba, the sign of Tfah, who bites into a grain with his teeth, does not come from it to be pickled ever, so far, and we were precisely chewing it, leaving it later, and not biting it, and refer to the sign of the NT, section 3:
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: [2] On his wound, etc.—Jewish chametz as 453 s.k. 5 general healing laws; Rokeach: even if chewed and placed before Passover requires destruction:
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: [3] For saliva, etc.—Rav's son-in-law Chok Yaakov: even blood flecks impossible without saliva as Yevamot 105—when sucking—end. Requires study Levush EH 169:40 first view even without sucking impossible without saliva; actually reason perhaps all blood valid for chalitzah; study: putrid moisture does not make fit per Machshirin poskim:
eliyah-rabbah/4:_: [4] And some stringent, etc.—extra zeal (Bach); Acharonim more stringent—give little by little so none remains:
eliyah-rabbah/5:_: [E] [clothing] there is metirin, etc. From the language of the Shulchan Aruch that he wrote from Metirin, it simply means to make it worse, and the opinion of the Shulchan Aruch means to make it worse, and the opinion of the Shulchan Aruch means to make it easier, and it is also proven from what I found in the requirement. This language seems to me. At Pesach, due to doubt, a sufficient person has to provide a sufficient person, which is permitted there in section 12, so far, the sweat of the wall is completely permitted, but in the Magan Avraham, Drov wrote Poskim forbidding and his words are not permissible for the spring. Also, what he wrote in allusions prohibits. In the basement and from the flask, he found wet wipes on the sack and prepared them from Danan Osparin. Chapter 2. The sweat of pit houses. And our religion in chapter 6. All the stock of fish in this sense of impurity is because of their decency, a stock in which there is water, and the other is the water that comes out of the eye, the water from the mouth, the water of the feet, whether large or small. In the matter of kosher there is no kai except in the thing called Mishka so far as the language of the book mentioned above on the parchment and from which you will learn many new laws. Jacob's Law wrote if one sweats from heat and wastes blood for all of us, one who misses:
eliyah-rabbah/6:_: [and] [wearing] the excrement of the roosters, etc. And the same is the case with Hittin, because of an animal (pharmacist), there is no sour water, discolored like blood and phlegm (Magan Avraham):

kaf-hachayyim/1:_: A) [Section 1] A person should not chew on teeth, etc., which means that it is permissible for him to chew and swallow immediately after tasting. MA SKA HI O. B. AR O. A. Makh O. B. HMM O. A. and 27. If he chews and engages in chewing, I do not bring it to Himmutz. AR stated in the name of Lehm Mishna 5:27. AA O. 1. and M.M. one should clean both of them afterwards so that nothing remains there and then he misses.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (2) There. Shall not chew, etc.—even less than kezayit—for though no lav by eating less than kezayit, perhaps Torah obligation destroy half-measure forbidden by Torah eating and retaining. Pri Chadash; however see Aruch HaShulchan 1 who lengthy wrote half-measure here only rabbinic; wrote permitted leave this melogma from nullified chametz if no kezayit—use on eve of holiday—end; see above 442 note 27:
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (3) There. Shall not chew wheat, etc.—meaning of melogma. Chafetz Chayim 1; see above 442 seif 2 and our words there:
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: d) Name. He should not chew, etc. And we were precisely in chewing, there is no acid in it, nor in biting an apple, and also in the bite of mice, there is no acid in it. 500 Hashaba C. Tfah A.R. O. A. A. A. O. A. and see above C. Tanag Sai' C. and in our words stated in the S.D.
kaf-hachayyim/5:_: e) Name. And he will give the adversary of his beating, etc., because they are soured by the saliva in his mouth when Shohin the adversary of the slaying is a mill lesson and goes through 2 and 2. If he has already chewed and laid down the adversary of a blow of KOP, he needs to be removed and removed. Pharmacist C. Ra'a. HI O. A. A. R. O. B. Makh O. A. R. 7 Ibid. And they should be removed when the hour comes that is sat in the A.P. but A. K. was already disgusted until she was disqualified from eating a dog in the C. T.M.B. R. I. Ibid. And Ish in Sai' 2 and in our words to that name in Sad.
kaf-hachayyim/6:_: (6) There. Place on wound—specifically Jewish chametz—bal yera'eh; but gentile chametz loaned to Jew or placed on wound without Jewish responsibility—permitted. If no melogma for gentile, Jew buys flour, gentile makes melogma for Jew's wound. Magen Avraham s.k. 2 in name of Kesef Mishneh chapter 5 Foundations Torah 8 in name of Orchot Chayim—see there; Matitei Yehuda 448:5 agrees; Rabbi Akiva Eiger 2; Rabbi Zalman 4; likewise above 465 note 6 in name of Acharonim—see there. However Makor Chayim 1 wondered on this permission—for when places on wound totally lost, not true loan returning—no greater gift—and therefore forbids unless spoilage in gentile hands before placing as 442 before placing—see there. Pri Chadash would not permit this case—see there; though Matitei Yehuda reconciled and agreed permit—nevertheless l'chatchila stringent if possible make so spoils in gentile hands before placing or knead fruit juice or other dressing; if impossible and great pain, rely on permitters; Jew intend not acquire at all, remains gentile property while on wound until thrown to trash:
